history.summary: West-facing stone Shiva temple ~1 km from the Bhoramdeo complex (Chaura/Bodla, near Kawardha), part of the same Bhoramdeo architectural tradition. Built by Phani Nagavanshi Gond king Ramchandra Dev; an inscription in the mandapa dates it to 1349 CE. 'Madwa' is a corruption of mandapa (the 16-pillared pillared hall, 31 ft square); 'Dulha Rao' (bridegroom) reflects local Gond belief that the hall was used for weddings — local lore says it commemorates the wedding of King Ramachandra Dev and Queen Ambika Devi in 1349. The lower sanctum houses a Shiva Linga with Nandi in the mandapa; external walls carry erotic/Kama Sutra-themed reliefs (~50-54 images) in concentric tiers, plus the usual tantric-era iconography of the Nagavanshi kings; a living temple popular with newly-married couples, and a state protected monument (ASI Chhattisgarh circle). CONFLICT FLAG: one travel site (vushii) claims a 5th century AD origin and another (chhattisgarhtours) an 11th-century origin — the 1349 CE inscription date per Wikipedia is the best-sourced and is used here. CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name; corrected to Chhattisgarh (state), town Kawardha, district Kabirdham.

name: Madwa Mahal Temple
town_description: Kawardha (officially Kabirdham) is the headquarters town of Kabirdham district in central Chhattisgarh, set at the foot of the Maikal hills; it is the gateway to the Bhoramdeo temple complex and the surrounding forested heritage belt.
